size_ceiling.model_context_source: read from the model's own GGUF header (model_header)
size_ceiling.why: the largest size 65536 comes from --sizes [32768, 65536]; it plus n_predict 16 fits the 131072-token per-slot ctx with 65520 tokens spare (--parallel 1), and the model's trained context read from its own GGUF header is 131072: the ceiling is a choice of what this run has to measure, not a model or ctx limit; a size that did not fit would be refused above, never truncated

provenance.argv_facts_source: parsed back out of the argv every arm receives (flags_from_argv), asserted equal per arm and against the intended flags before the first engine
provenance.sleep_idle_note: short so the release lands inside the run; the app ships 300
provenance.max_load_note: gate on the 1-minute load average, checked before any engine starts; 0 disables it and would be recorded as 0.0
provenance.warm_threshold_kind: RULE - the line this verdict draws, not a measured datum
provenance.wall_times_note: wall times are measurements of this machine at nice 10 under whatever else it was doing, not performance promises
provenance.invariant_note: contention-invariant: token counts, cache_n, file bytes. NOT invariant: prompt_ms, save_ms, every wall - they move with loadavg_before (recorded above and below) and are labelled wherever they are quoted
provenance.refusal_semantics: EXIT 0 means the artifact was written. A measurement that is invalid is refused INSIDE the artifact, not by the exit code: the arm carries measured=false with its blockers and the conclusion begins 'no verdict: ...' - this harness's deliverable is the evidence of WHY a run failed, and a non-zero exit would make that record look like a crash and invite a re-run that overwrites it. The two gates are the exceptions: --max-load and the headroom check exit non-zero BEFORE anything is measured, and write no artifact

ctx_measurement_caveat.note: MEASURED AT ctx_size 131072, NOT at the app's default 65536: a 65536-token chat + n_predict 16 needs 65552 tokens, which the app's default does NOT fit - the headroom gate refuses rather than truncates - so this run used 131072 with 65520 tokens of headroom. Per-token figures are ctx-independent by the committed evidence: the same 53,352 B/token slope at ctx 8192 (dev/results/unload-restore-release) and ctx 16384 (dev/results/unload-restore-disk-curve).

disk_law.formula: bytes = per_layer_bpt x (layer_full x tokens + 2 x layer_windowed x min(tokens, window))

verdict.conclusion: after a real release the saved chats came back warm and the no-file controls stayed cold, so the warmth travelled with the file. Numbers: 32768 tokens: saved cache_n=32763/32768 n_restored=32783 restore=791.97ms (resident 53.58ms, reload est. 677.5ms), control cache_n=0/32768; 65536 tokens: saved cache_n=65531/65536 n_restored=65551 restore=843.63ms (resident 106.35ms, reload est. 676.8ms), control cache_n=0/65536 | disk curve: (a) bytes/token: 32768 tokens -> 343836904 B = 10493 B/token; 65536 tokens -> 593922280 B = 9063 B/token (marginal 32768->65536: 7632 B/token); the 600->1900 base was 53352 B/token, the q8_0 full-KV arithmetic from the model's own GGUF header is 30464 B/token. THE KNEE LIES BELOW THE SMALLEST SIZE MEASURED HERE (32768 tokens): that interval's marginal already reads 7632 B/token against the 53352 below-window base, so the 2048-token window was crossed between 1900 (the base's upper end, measured in the companion 600/1900 artifact) and 32768 tokens. THAT INTERVAL IS ALREADY BEYOND THE KNEE: its marginal 7632 B/token IS the post-window slope - the 14 full layers x 544 = 7616 B/token (measured 7632) - so the slope is flat past the knee and NO further bend is announced in this range. (b) benefit per size: 32768 tokens: 25800.913 ms cold re-prefill vs 72.62 ms warm -> 25728.3 ms avoided, 32763/32768 tokens reused; 65536 tokens: 71044.653 ms cold re-prefill vs 92.124 ms warm -> 70952.5 ms avoided, 65531/65536 tokens reused - the MILLISECOND half is this machine at this load (contention-dependent, not a promise); the invariant half is the token count and the byte counts above; the benefit grows FASTER than with the token count (0.785 -> 1.083 ms avoided per token, 32768 -> 65536 tokens). (c) this artifact does not reach 4096 tokens (sizes: 32768, 65536), so the plan's ~218 MB at 4096 is NOT settled here - it is settled by the artifact that measures 4096. (d) at 65536 tokens there is NO excess: the file sits 21401 B/token BELOW the header's full-KV arithmetic, which is what the 2048-token window capping the windowed layers does to a file. The positive excess exists only BELOW the window; it is measured and attributed in the companion 600/1900-token artifact (dev/results/unload-restore-release), not re-derived from this one. (e) the law read from the model's own header - 2048-token window, 14 full + 42 windowed layers from the boot lines, 544 B/layer/token, layers sum to 56 blocks (True): 32768: predicted 343146496 B vs measured 343836904 B (+0.20 %); 65536: predicted 592707584 B vs measured 593922280 B (+0.20 %) -> the law HOLDS within 0.2 % at every size (f) THE NUMBER FOR THE OWNER: one chat saved at the app's default context (65536 tokens, read from crates/kalsa-launch/src/args.rs) costs MEASURED 593922280 bytes = 593.9 MB; BY ARITHMETIC ON THAT MEASUREMENT, not measured as a group, the menu offers 1/2/4 devices (read from crates/kalsa-launch/src/policy/menu.rs), so saved chats alone are 1 = 593.9 MB, 2 = 1187.8 MB, 4 = 2375.7 MB
